result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.resistance_distance_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate the resistance distance matrix for all node pairs. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24956-L25006){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.resistance_distance_matrix() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Returns a dictionary mapping (source_id, target_id) tuples to their resistance distances. The matrix is symmetric with zeros on the diagonal. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[tuple[int, int], float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping node ID pairs to resistance distances. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Builds the full symmetric matrix of pairwise effective resistances in a single $O(n^3)$ computation of the Laplacian pseudoinverse $L^+$, from which every entry is recovered as $\Omega(u, v) = L^+_{uu} + L^+_{vv} - 2 L^+_{uv}$. That shared-cost structure makes the matrix substantially cheaper than $\binom{n}{2}$ individual `get_resistance_distance()` calls whenever more than a handful of pairs are needed. The returned dictionary contains both orientations for every ordered pair for lookup convenience; entries on the diagonal are $0$. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The matrix is symmetric, so the resistance between any two nodes is the same regardless of direction: ::: {#d3cf4a38 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph() g.add_path_graph(3) matrix = g.resistance_distance_matrix() # Returns 2.0 matrix[(1, 3)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2.0 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#da12c6c3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns True: the matrix is symmetric matrix[(1, 2)] == matrix[(2, 1)] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: :::
